{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Davison "Dave" Eugene Soper''' (21 March 1943, [[Milwaukee, Wisconsin]]) is an American [[theoretical physicist]] specializing in [[high energy physics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Davison E. Soper's page |url=https://pages.uoregon.edu/soper/ |access-date=2025-12-13 |website=pages.uoregon.edu}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Soper received his bachelor's degree in 1965 from [[Amherst College]], and his PhD in 1971 under [[James Bjorken]] at [[Stanford University]], where he worked with [[John Kogut]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Kogut, J.B.|author2=Soper, D.E.|title=Quantum electrodynamics in the infinite-momentum frame|journal=Physical Review D|date=15 May 1970|volume=1|issue=10|pages=2901–2914|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.1.2901|bibcode=1970PhRvD...1.2901K |osti=1444761}}</ref> From 1971 to 1973 Soper was an instructor, and from 1973 to 1977 an assistant professor at [[Princeton University]]. He was appointed in 1977–80 an assistant professor, in 1980–83 an associate professor, and from 1983 to the present a professor at the [[University of Oregon]], where from 2004 to 2007 he was chair of the physics department.<ref>[http://pages.uoregon.edu/soper/vita.pdf Vita, Davison E. Soper]</ref>

His doctoral dissertation on ''Null Plane Field Theory'' dealt with the theory of high energy scattering processes in the [[parton model]]. With [[George Sterman]] and [[John C. Collins]], he proved a factorization theorem in perturbative [[quantum chromodynamics]] (QCD).<ref>{{cite journal|author=Collins, John C.|author2=Soper, Davison E.|author3=Sterman, George|title=Factorization for short distance hadron-hadron scattering|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=281|year=1985|pages=104–142|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(85)90565-6|bibcode=1985NuPhB.261..104C |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book
  | author= John C. Collins, Davison E. Soper and George Sterman
  | editor-first = A. H
  | editor-last = Mueller
  | editor-link=Alfred Mueller
  | year = 1989
  | chapter = Factorization of Hard Processes in QCD
  | title = Perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics
  | publisher = World Scientific
  | pages = 1–92
  | isbn =9789971505646
  | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=61cPPKtCsNoC&pg=PA1
}}</ref>

Soper is a member of the "Coordinated Theoretical-Experimental Project on QCD" (CTEQ), whose co-spokesperson he was from 2001 to 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |last=The CTEQ Collaboration |date=March 22, 2022 |title=A History of CTEQ: The Coordinated Project on Theoretical and Experimental Studies of QCD |url=https://www.physics.smu.edu/scalise/cteq/History/history.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240616065547/https://www.physics.smu.edu/scalise/cteq/History/history.pdf |archive-date=Jun 16, 2024 |access-date=December 12, 2025 |website=SMU Physics}}</ref> He was on the editorial board of ''[[Physical Review Letters]]''<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2011 |title=Physical Review Letters Editorial Board  (Divisional Associate Editors) |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/issues/106/4/deliverables/masthead/print |journal=Physical Review Letters}}</ref> and ''[[Physical Review D]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1998 |title=Physical Review D: Particles, Fields, Gravitation and Cosmology |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/issues/57/4/deliverables/masthead/print |journal=Physical Review D}}</ref>

== Honors ==

* The [[Sakurai Prize]] of the [[American Physical Society]]., 2009, with [[Richard Keith Ellis|R. Keith Ellis]] and [[John C. Collins]], ''For work in perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics, including applications to problems pivotal to the interpretation of high energy particle collisions''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prize Recipient |url=https://aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Davison&last_nm=Soper&year=2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240304003916/https://aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Davison&last_nm=Soper&year=2009 |archive-date=2024-03-04 |access-date=2025-12-13 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>
* Fellow, American Physical Society, 2010, cited ''For seminal work in Perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics, especially proving theorems on factorization which play a crucial role in interpreting high energy particle collisions.''<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2010&unit_id=DPF&institution=University+of+Oregon|url-status=live|access-date=2021-07-17|website=www.aps.org|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210717054738/https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2010&unit_id=DPF&institution=University+of+Oregon |archive-date=2021-07-17 }}</ref>
